summary: Texas Tech lost 37-24 at Cincinnati. Run defense, red-zone finishing and penalties lead the corrections before Arizona visits Saturday in the early television window.

items.headline: Texas Tech takes its first loss, 37-24 at Cincinnati
items.tldr: The Red Raiders return home after a difficult road outing. Use the next possessions to judge the corrections rather than treating the unbeaten start as a complete description of the team.
items.outlet: Associated Press via Texas Tech Athletics

items.headline: Tabb runs for 173 yards against Texas Tech
items.tldr: Cincinnati’s backfield kept the offense moving. Watch the edge and cutback fits before judging whether another defensive pass rush can rescue a long down.

items.headline: Cincinnati finishes its red-zone chances with touchdowns
items.tldr: The Bearcats’ four red-zone visits produced four passing scores. Texas Tech needs coverage that survives the route break when the field narrows.

items.headline: Texas Tech commits 12 penalties for 80 yards
items.tldr: The official postgame notes put discipline alongside the three turnovers as costs of the loss. Keep the formation, snap and contact legal before chasing the next explosive play.

items.headline: Arizona visits Texas Tech at 11 a.m. CT Saturday
items.tldr: The October 31 kickoff is set. Use the schedule panel for the updated ESPN assignment after the original announcement left the network open.

lead.headline: Close the lane before chasing the play.
lead.body: Hold the edge and keep the cutback fit connected to the inside pursuit. On offense, protect the possession with legal alignment and a first receiving answer that does not require another extended down.

matchup.thesis: Make the next down earned, not donated
matchup.question: What should fans watch in the next game?
matchup.answer: Defend the run with clear gap responsibility and carry red-zone routes through their breaks. Keep offensive penalties from undoing a clean gain before the next call arrives.

signals.title: Run-defense fits
signals.detail: Watch the edge defender and the next inside gap together. Pursuit should close behind the first tackle rather than open a new lane across the formation.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with run-defense fits?

signals.title: Red-zone coverage
signals.detail: Keep leverage when the receiver changes direction near the goal line. Make the quarterback throw through coverage that lasts the whole down.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with red-zone coverage?

signals.title: Penalty discipline
signals.detail: Get the alignment and snap settled, then keep blocks controlled through contact. A well-designed play needs every assignment to survive the officials’ view.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with penalty discipline?

signals.title: Ball security
signals.detail: Give pressure a quick outlet and secure the ball through the exchange. Do not let one difficult down donate another possession to the opponent.
